page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.2xlarge is a storage-focused virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor with an x86_64 architecture, providing 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU operates at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz and includes a 33 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. A defining characteristic of this instance is its massive bundled local storage, consisting of 23,622 GB of HDD capacity. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the ecs.d1.2xlarge is positioned in the lower tier for compute-heavy workloads. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests, such as stress-ng and Geekbench, place the instance in the bottom 25% category. Memory bandwidth tests for read-only operations also rank in the bottom 25%, although large-block write operations achieve average performance. Cryptographic and compression tasks show lower efficiency, with single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression scoring in the bottom 10%. Passmark CPU and extended instruction tests perform at an average level, while database operations and Redis SET operations remain in the bottom 25%.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.d1.2xlarge is its reliance on legacy HDD local storage and older Intel Xeon architecture, which limits its suitability for high-IOPS databases or intensive real-time processing. However, it offers high resource density for cold storage and sequential data access. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the instance provides an exceptionally large storage-to-compute ratio, making it a viable option for workloads requiring massive data capacity without demanding high CPU performance. Appropriate workloads include data archiving, log storage, distributed file systems, and offline batch processing where storage volume is prioritized over high-speed random I/O.

Running on the KVM hypervisor, it is equipped with an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor offering 8 dedicated vCPUs, 4 physical cores, and a 2.5 GHz clock speed. The system includes 32.0 GB of RAM and a massive 23,622 GB of local HDD storage, alongside a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps. Benchmark results indicate modest compute capabilities, with single-core and multi-core performance generally ranking in the bottom 25%, though large-block memory write speeds and Passmark CPU scores reach average levels. Given its legacy HDD storage and lower compute performance, this instance is best suited for workloads prioritizing high storage capacity over rapid processing, such as data archiving, log analysis, and distributed file systems.
